scenario: A male patient of unknown age is found in an alley with severe altered level of consciousness and tachypnea. The scenario focuses on broad workup, airway protection, recognition of severe anion gap and osmolar gap metabolic acidosis, and treatment for suspected toxic alcohol ingestion.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: GCS 3, he can't protect his airway. Set up for RSI and intubation now. Bag him with the BVM before I attempt.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Pre-oxygenated with BVM, RSI meds pushed, tube's in. Ready for confirmation and securing.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Tube's in. Get me a post-intubation chest X-ray to confirm placement.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send toxicology and osmolality. He's comatose with no clear cause, so I want to rule out a toxic ingestion.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Send a basic metabolic panel too. I need it to work up a metabolic cause for the coma and calculate the gap.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Results back: post-intubation CXR done. Tox and osmolality: osmol 339, EtOH under 2, ASA and APA negative. So elevated osmolality with a negative alcohol level. BMP still pending, ready in about two turns for your gap.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start fomepizole now for suspected toxic alcohol ingestion. Osmolality's 339 with EtOH under 2, so that gap isn't from alcohol. BMP's still pending for the anion gap, but I'm not waiting to treat.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Fomepizole is in and running.

available_results.result: Post-intubation CXR.

available_results.name: Toxicology and osmolality
available_results.result: Osmol 339, EtOH <2, ASA neg, APA neg.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: BMP's back: HCO3 10, anion gap 25 with a Cr of 98. High anion gap metabolic acidosis confirms the toxic alcohol picture. Fomepizole running. You want me to line up dialysis or a bicarb order?

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start sodium bicarbonate now for the severe metabolic acidosis, HCO3 is 10. And get nephrology on the phone for urgent dialysis.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a venous blood gas now so I can track his pH and see how the acidosis responds to the bicarb.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: VBG's back: pH 7.10, PCO2 22, HCO3 10, lactate 4. Still severely acidotic despite the bicarb. He's vented at RR 12 on the set rate. BP 98/62, HR 106, sat 97 percent.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Bump the vent rate up. His pH is still 7.10 despite the bicarb, so I need more minute ventilation to help compensate. Dialysis is still the definitive fix here, so keep pushing nephrology.
